package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	type key int
	const k key = 1
	p := context.WithValue(context.Background(), k, 9)
	c, cancel := context.WithCancel(p)
	defer cancel()
	d := context.WithoutCancel(c)
	cancel()
	fmt.Println(d.Value(k).(int))
}
What key type is recommended for WithValue?
options: A string with a unique package prefix

questions.text: What does context.Cause return after WithCancel with no cause?
options: The same error as Err(), usually Canceled

questions.text: What does context.WithoutCancel do?
options: Derives a child that is not canceled with the parent

questions.text: When does an AfterFunc callback run if the context is already done?
options: Only if cancel is called again

questions.text: Can a child WithDeadline extend the parent deadline?
options: Yes, if the child is created from Background

questions.text: What happens to a child derived from an already canceled parent?
options: Err() stays nil until its own cancel

questions.text: Why must you still call the cancel from WithTimeout?
options: Otherwise the timer may live until expiry and hold resources
Otherwise the program does not compile

questions.text: Why should two packages not share the same string key?
What is the cause in WithCancelCause?
options: The reason error that context.Cause returns

questions.text: Does WithoutCancel drop parent values?
options: No. Values remain; cancellation does not
Only if the parent is already canceled

questions.text: What does AfterFunc’s stop return if the callback has not started?
options: false, and the callback still runs
true, and the callback will not run

questions.text: Does WithCancel inherit the parent deadline?
options: Only if you call the parent Deadline() yourself

questions.text: Should you put an optional function parameter in Value?
options: No. It is not for API parameters
Yes, if the key is a string

What does WithTimeoutCause add over WithTimeout?
options: It changes Err() to the cause
It sets the Cause when the deadline fires

questions.text: Are two different unexported types with the same number the same key?
options: Yes, the underlying int is compared
Yes, if the values are equal
No. The key type is part of the comparison
